data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference of future truth, but as a non-inductive methodological rule for maximizing the content of our conjectures; however, accepting this defense costs us the ability to claim rational assurance that acting on such theories will succeed in practical applications (e.g., bridge building), reducing the preference to a bold gamble rather than a justified expectation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration can be shown to logically entail a higher degree of verisimilitude (truth-likeness) that is calculable, the 'gamble' characterization fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's own writings on 'acting on' theories explicitly invoke a principle of induction under a different name, the defense collapses into self-contradiction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a non-inductive metric for practical reliability (distinct from truth-content) can be derived strictly from falsificationist premises, the 'cost' of lacking assurance is paid.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The argument distinguishes between 'logical probability' (which Popper rejects as increasing with corroboration) and 'methodological utility' (choosing the theory with the highest empirical content and severest test survival). It posits that preferring the better-corroborated theory is rational because it offers the most informative potential falsification, not because it is likely true. The 'cost' is identified as the inability to bridge the gap between this methodological choice and pragmatic safety, forcing a concession that action based on corroboration remains logically indistinguishable from action based on any other unrefuted theory regarding future success.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
